overview.en: Pieter Zeeman was a Dutch physicist who discovered the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field, known as the Zeeman effect. This discovery provided crucial evidence for the electron theory of matter. He shared the 1902 Nobel Prize in Physics with Hendrik Lorentz.

early_life.en: Zeeman was born in Zonnemaire, Netherlands, a small village in Zeeland. He studied physics at the University of Leiden under Hendrik Lorentz and Heike Kamerlingh Onnes, completing his doctorate in 1893.

impact.en: The Zeeman effect was instrumental in confirming the existence of electron spin and understanding atomic structure. It became a powerful tool in spectroscopy and astrophysics for measuring magnetic fields. His work supported the classical electron theory of Lorentz and paved the way for quantum mechanics.

event.en: Discovered the splitting of spectral lines in a magnetic field (Zeeman effect).
Appointed professor of physics at the University of Amsterdam.
Awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics jointly with Hendrik Lorentz.
Became director of the newly built Zeeman Laboratory in Amsterdam.

title.en: On the Influence of Magnetism on the Nature of the Light Emitted by a Substance

description.en: Paper describing the discovery of the Zeeman effect.
Comprehensive account of his experimental work on the interaction of light and magnetism.

text.en: It was in the autumn of 1896 that I conceived the idea of making an experiment to decide the question of the influence of magnetism on the nature of light.
